lines.text: A camera photo takes time: take it, process it, send it over the network. A few hundredths of a second.
At driving speed, the robot moves about five centimeters in that time. Draw the tag from where the robot is now, and it lands five centimeters wrong.
So every photo carries its age. The robot rewinds its memory to the moment the photo was taken, and draws the tag from there.
Photos older than a quarter of a second are thrown away.
